mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the combined signal fails to outperform a flat benchmark.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months, accompanied by a stable or falling unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals robust labor market expansion that supports corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE <= previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains unchanged signals inflation surprise and potential future tightening, which increases term premium and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.4% AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 65% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly rise of more than 2% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically above zero in at least 70% of triggered months.
